summary: There are two independent problems. (1) Token cost and slowness: llm-gateway tokens_per_min rose from about 42k to a 400000 ceiling starting around 10:50-11:00 UTC, while orchestrator began logging 'agent loop detected: repeated tool call get_holdings x38' at 10:55:20. This points to an orchestrator agent tool-call loop burning LLM tokens. llm-gateway is a victim of that load, not the cause. portfolio-svc looks healthy, and no deploy, config or flag change landed near onset, so what triggered the loop is not established. (2) Blank notifications: the msg-delivery deploy at 11:24 ('notification template refactor') was followed from 11:25:18 by 'template render failed: missing variable portfolio_value' and redeliveries on outbound-msgs. That matches the blank or failed notifications and is separate from the token problem.

hypotheses.statement: The orchestrator agent repeatedly calls get_holdings in a loop, driving runaway LLM token use, slowness and the token-cost alert. llm-gateway is saturated as a consequence.
hypotheses.label: medium

supporting.text: llm-gateway tokens_per_min jumped from about 42k to 131k in the 10:50 bucket, then pinned at 400000
Earliest orchestrator agent loop error in the window, at 10:55:20; the query ended 10:56 and returned only 3 hits
orchestrator calls llm-gateway with the highest weight, so loop traffic flows into the gateway
llm-gateway latency is elevated but its error and parse-failure rates are low, which fits load rather than a gateway fault

contradicting.text: portfolio-svc, the get_holdings backend, shows normal latency and error rate, so it is not the failing dependency

hypotheses.statement: The msg-delivery template refactor deploy (msg-delivery-00290) removed or renamed the portfolio_value variable, so notifications fail to render or go out blank. This is independent of the token spike.
hypotheses.label: medium

unresolved: What triggered the get_holdings loop: no deploy, config or flag change near 10:50-10:55 explains it, and the metrics-label-rename deploys at 10:12-10:25 are unproven as related.

The loop errors were seen in a truncated log result (180 total, 50 returned), so the true start time and number of affected sessions are not confirmed. The 10:50 token bucket may begin slightly before 10:55:20.
Whether the 400000 tokens_per_min is a provider or gateway cap, and how much real demand is being throttled.
The msg-delivery logs were truncated (60 total), and the exact count of blank notifications was not measured.
Whether the token spike and the blank notifications interact, for example blank messages causing user retries, was not tested.

actions.text: Roll back msg-delivery to the release before msg-delivery-00290, or hotfix the template to supply portfolio_value.
actions.rationale: Render errors started about 1 minute after the deploy and match the blank notifications.

actions.text: Cap per-session tool calls in orchestrator (the loop guard aborts only at x38) and add a per-user or global token budget and rate limit on llm-gateway to stop the cost burn.
actions.rationale: Tokens are pinned at 400000 per minute, driven by looping sessions.

actions.text: Inspect orchestrator get_holdings call and response payloads for a few looping sessions, along with the prompt and tool definitions, to find why the model keeps re-calling it. Check whether the tool result shape changed.
actions.rationale: portfolio-svc is healthy and no change correlates with onset, so the trigger is unknown.

actions.text: Confirm the outbound-msgs backlog and redelivery loop drain after the msg-delivery fix, and resend or suppress the failed notifications.
actions.rationale: Redelivered messages indicate repeated failures on outbound-msgs.

actions.text: Add a deploy-time template variable contract test for msg-delivery and an alert on agent-loop error rate.
actions.rationale: Both failures were detected only through user reports or cost alerts.
